'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***A female [[Afghan National Police|police]] officer is killed by gunmen in the city of [[Jalalabad]], [[Nangarhar]], during an increase of targeted killings of women in the city. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attacks-idUSKBN2BO59P (Reuters)]
*Spillover of the [[Colombian conflict]]
**[[2021 Apure clashes]]
***Two [[Venezuelan Army]] troops are killed and nine others are wounded by a [[land mine]], near the [[Colombia–Venezuela border|border]] with [[Colombia]], during operations against [[Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia|FARC]] dissidents and other "irregular armed groups". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-colombia-venezuela/venezuela-says-two-soldiers-killed-by-land-mine-near-colombia-border-idUSKBN2BP05P?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Terrorism in Burkina Faso]]
**Six [[auxiliaries]] of the [[Burkina Faso Armed Forces]] are killed in an [[ambush]] during an operation in [[Dablo Department|Dablo]], [[Sanmatenga Province|Sanmatenga]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/six-killed-in-attack-in-northern-burkina-faso-01617357008?tesla=y (''Barron's'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the music industry]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]], [[Eurovision Song Contest 2021]]
**The [[Government of the Netherlands|government]] announces that it will permit the attendance of around 3,500 fans into [[Rotterdam Ahoy]] for the Eurovision contest on May 18–22, as part of a trial to reopen public venues. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/dutch-to-let-fans-attend-eurovision-in-covid-trial (Radio France Internationale)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Minimum wage in New Zealand]]
**[[New Zealand]] raises its [[minimum wage]] to [[New Zealand dollar|$]]20 per hour, increasing the average income of 175,500 citizens by $44 per week, while income tax on those earning over $180,000 rises to 39 percent. [[Welfare]] spending, student allowances, and support for first time home buyers are also increased. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/australasia/new-zealand-raises-minimum-wage-to-20-an-hour-b1825634.html (''The Independent'')]
*The [[S&P 500]] closes its [[trading day]] at 4,019.87, the first time it ended at above 4,000. [https://www.straitstimes.com/business/companies-markets/sp-500-ends-above-4000-for-first-time (''The Straits Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Sixteen people are killed after a bus collided with a semi-trailer truck in [[Ivory Coast]], [[West Africa]]. [https://www.afrikmag.com/cote-divoire-grave-accident-entre-ferke-et-ouangolo-bilan-provisoire-16-morts/ (Afrikmag)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 6,469 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, prompting the [[Government of Bangladesh|government]] to impose a series of new measures, including banning all travellers from the [[European Union]] and 12 other countries for two weeks beginning April 3. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/1/bangladesh-witnesses-a-record-surge-in-coronavirus-cases (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Phnom Penh]] imposes a curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time that suspends all non-essential business activities and gatherings for two weeks in order to prevent the spread of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.khmertimeskh.com/50833024/phnom-penh-placed-under-curfew-for-two-weeks-effective-today/ (''Khmer Times'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The [[Government of Japan|Japanese government]] designates [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]], [[Hyogo Prefecture|Hyogo]], and [[Miyagi Prefecture]]s for tougher measures against COVID-19 amid a rise in cases. The measures include fines of [[Japanese yen|¥]]200,000 ([[US dollar|$]]1,808.80) for restaurants and bars that ignore mandates to shorten operating hours to 8:00 p.m., and capping attendance of large events to 5,000 people. These measures will be effective for one month beginning on April 5. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/04/e047dcab633f-japan-govt-to-let-osaka-hyogo-miyagi-take-stricter-virus-steps.html (Kyodo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports nine locally transmitted cases of the 501.V2 variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]], which was originally detected in [[South Africa]]. [https://www.malaysiakini.com/news/569083 (''Malaysiakini'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] receives the first batch consisting 811,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] distributed through [[COVAX]] scheme. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-vietnam-covax-idUSKBN2BO4HN (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra]]
****[[Andorra]] receives 30.000 doses of Oxford-Astrazenca vaccines from [[COVAX]] [[WHO]] program. [https://www.diariandorra.ad/noticies/nacional/2021/04/01/andorra_rep_000_vacunes_astrazeneca_177505_1125.html (''Diari d'Andorra'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[Prime Minister of France|Prime Minister]] [[Jean Castex]] announces a ban of alcoholic drinks in parks and outdoor public spaces in [[France]] as part of the limited nationwide lockdown to curb the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/france-to-ban-outdoor-drinking-under-new-coronavirus-restrictions (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[President of Germany|President]] [[Frank-Walter Steinmeier]] receives his first dose of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/german-president-steinmeier-receives-astrazeneca-jab-01617272106 (''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Moldova]]
****[[Moldova]] enters a 60-day [[state of emergency]] to reduce the spread of COVID-19. Acting [[Prime Minister of Moldova|Prime Minister]] [[Aureliu Ciocoi]] says that the rate of infection has increased to 635 per 100,000 people. [https://www.rferl.org/a/moldova-covid-state-emergency-sandu-criticism-snap-elections/31180618.html (Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] breaks vaccination record with 306,000 doses injected in one day. [https://elpais.com/sociedad/2021-04-01/espana-bate-su-record-de-vacunas-puestas-en-un-dia-con-306000-dosis-inyectadas.html (''El País'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports a record 40,806 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3.3 million. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/turkey-reports-record-40-800-new-covid-19-cases/2195647 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[Governor of California|California Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] receives the [[Johnson & Johnson]] [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.sfchronicle.com/politics/article/Newsom-gets-his-Johnson-Johnson-COVID-shot-as-16070048.php (''San Francisco Chronicle'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****[[Michigan]] reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant in a person from [[Bay County, Michigan|Bay County]]. [https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/michigan/2021/04/01/michigan-identifies-first-case-covid-19-p-1-variant-brazil/4834794001/ (''Detroit News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|Lockdown]] restrictions are eased in [[Queensland]], including [[Brisbane]], after a decline in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/coronavirus-queensland-update-brisbane-lockdown-to-end-one-new-locally-acquired-covid19-case-latest-numbers/6c1ec6ba-930f-4c72-801e-2893a9bd0cc0 (''Nine News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Chile]]
***After surpassing one million cases, the [[Government of Chile|government]] announces several new restrictions. Borders will be closed for 30 days; the curfew will start one hour earlier; work permits during [[quarantine]] will be given only for essential activities; and sales will be permitted only for food, medicine, and hygiene products.  [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/chile-to-close-borders-ratchet-up-controls-in-april-as-covid-19-14540240 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***The [[South African Health Products Regulatory Authority]] approves the general use of the single-dose Johnson & Johnson [[vaccine]]. [https://businesstech.co.za/news/government/480685/johnson-johnson-covid-vaccine-approved-for-general-use-in-south-africa/amp/ (Business Tech)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]]
****Pfizer announces a revised efficacy rating of 91.3% for its vaccine candidate, down from its original rating of 95%, and affirms that protection afforded by the vaccine lasts for at least six months. Pfizer also announces that the vaccine appeared to provide protection against the [[501.V2 variant]] in 100% of cases during its South African trial run. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/04/01/pfizer-covid-vaccine-is-91percent-effective-in-updated-data-protective-against-south-african-variant.html (CNBC)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]], [[Myanmar–United Kingdom relations]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] places sanctions on Burmese conglomerate [[Myanmar Economic Corporation]] for funding the junta and for associating with military officials. British Foreign Secretary [[Dominic Raab]] also accuses the junta of "sinking to a new low with the wanton killing of innocent people, including children". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics-britain/uk-sanctions-myanmar-conglomerate-says-junta-sinking-to-new-lows-with-killings-idUSKBN2BO53U?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Taiwan–United States relations]]
**[[List of ambassadors of the United States to Palau|U.S. ambassador to Palau]] [[John Hennessey-Niland]] becomes the first sitting American envoy to visit [[Taiwan]] since the U.S. cut formal ties in 1979. The visit coincided with the opening of a COVID-19 "[[travel bubble]]" between Taiwan and [[Palau]]. The highest level visit in 42 years prompted anger from [[China]], who warned the U.S. against "[[One-China policy|crossing its red line]]". [https://thediplomat.com/2021/04/us-ambassador-makes-first-visit-to-taiwan-in-more-than-40-years/ (''The Diplomat'')] [https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/china/china-taiwan-visit-us-ambassador-b1824196.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**[[Russia]]n [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Russia)|Minister of Foreign Affairs]] [[Sergey Lavrov]] warns of a rising "anti-[[White people|White]]" racism in the [[United States]], saying that [[political correctness]] was being "taken to the extreme". Lavrov also accuses the U.S. of attempting to spread a [[List of cultural, intellectual, philosophical and technological revolutions|cultural revolution]] around the world. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/04/01/russia-warns-of-anti-white-aggression-in-us-a73446 (''The Moscow Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]]
**A [[Judiciary of Hong Kong|Hong Kong court]] convicts nine activists of the opposition [[Pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|pro-democracy camp]] for organizing and participating in an "[[Public Order Ordinance|unlawful assembly]]". Among those convicted are politicians [[Martin Lee]], [[Leung Kwok-hung]], and [[Margaret Ng]], and entrepreneur [[Jimmy Lai]]. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1413688/9-veteran-hong-kong-activists-convicted-over-huge-democracy-rally (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*[[Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**Three [[Federal Police (Belgium)|Belgian police]] officers are injured and four people are arrested, after a crowd of around 2,000 people at the [[Bois de la Cambre]] park in [[Brussels]] is charged for violating [[Social distancing measures related to the COVID-19 pandemic|social distancing measures]] by organizing and participating in a [[coronavirus party]] marketed as an [[April Fools' Day]] prank. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/2093751/police-charge-brussels-april-fools-day-party-crowd (''The Bangkok Post'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[President of Slovakia|Slovak President]] [[Zuzana Čaputová]] appoints Finance Minister [[Eduard Heger]] as the new [[Prime Minister of Slovakia|Prime Minister]], ending a month-long political crisis. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-slovakia-government/slovak-president-appoints-eduard-heger-as-prime-minister-idUSKBN2BO4PS?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Gian Carlo Venturini]] and [[Marco Nicolini]] are sworn in as the new [[Captains Regent]] of [[San Marino]], succeeding [[Alessandro Cardelli]] and [[Mirko Dolcini]]. [https://www.sanmarinortv.sm/news/attualita-c4/alessandro-cardelli-e-mirko-dolcini-sono-i-nuovi-capitani-reggenti-a194943 (San Marino RTV)]
